title: Constant Reciprocity in Function Fields
content: Hilbert's Ninth Problem sought the most general reciprocity law; the parent gallery entry closes by asking what reciprocity phenomena exist in function fields. In F_q[T] (q an odd prime power), the monic irreducibles P play the role of the primes and the quadratic residue symbol (a/P) is computed in the residue field F_q[T]/(P) ≅ F_{q^{deg P}}. For a CONSTANT a ∈ F_q^× the classical constant reciprocity law says (a/P) = χ_q(a)^{deg P} — equivalently, a constant that is a nonsquare in F_q becomes a square in F_{q^d} exactly when d is even. This file formalizes that as a relation between the quadratic characters of a finite field F and any finite extension K.

title: Characteristic Transfer and {±1}-Cast Injectivity
content: Two helper lemmas make the descent rigorous. cast_pm_inj: integers drawn from {1,−1} that agree after casting into a field of characteristic ≠ 2 are equal — this is exactly the injectivity needed to pass from an equality of character VALUES in K back to an equality of integers (using Ring.neg_one_ne_one_of_char_ne_two). ringChar_extension_ne_two: the algebra map F → K is injective (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective), so charP_of_injective_algebraMap transfers F's characteristic to K; hence odd characteristic of F passes to K, letting Euler's criterion be applied in K.
mathContext: $\mathrm{ringChar}\,K = \mathrm{ringChar}\,F \ne 2$, and $1 \ne -1$ in $K$ forces $\{\pm 1\}$-valued casts to be injective.

title: Reconciling the Two Euler Exponents via the Geometric Sum
content: Euler's criterion gives χ_F(a) = a^{q/2} in F and χ_K(A) = A^{(q^d)/2} in K, where q = |F|, A = algebraMap a, d = [K:F]. The exponents are reconciled by the Nat identity card K / 2 = (q/2)·S with S = 1 + q + … + q^{d−1}: from |K| = q^d, the geometric factorization (q−1)·S = q^d − 1 (Nat.geomSum_eq + Nat.sub_dvd_pow_sub_pow), and 2·(q/2) = q − 1 for odd q. So A^{|K|/2} = (A^{q/2})^S. Since (A^{q/2})² = A^{q−1} = 1 (Fermat in a finite field), the value A^{q/2} is a sign whose power depends only on the exponent's parity.

title: The Sign Is the Parity of the Degree
content: The whole reciprocity sign collapses to deg-parity. Because q is odd, every q^i is odd, so S = Σ q^i ≡ d (mod 2) (Finset.sum_nat_mod). For a unit u with u² = 1, uⁿ depends only on n mod 2, giving (A^{q/2})^S = (A^{q/2})^d. Casting back and using cast_pm_inj plus the quadratic-character dichotomy (χ values lie in {±1}) descends the K-equality to the integer identity χ_K(A) = χ_F(a)^d. The final case split handles χ_F(a) = 1 (any power is 1) and χ_F(a) = −1 (the power is (−1)^d, by even/odd d).
mathContext: $S \equiv d \pmod 2$ since each $q^i$ is odd, so $(A^{q/2})^S = (A^{q/2})^d$ and $\chi_K(A) = \chi_F(a)^d$.

title: Square Criterion and the Even-Degree Corollary
content: isSquare_algebraMap_iff reads the reciprocity law through quadraticChar_one_iff_isSquare: a nonzero constant a is a square in K iff a is already a square in F (χ_F(a) = 1) or [K:F] is even — because a nonsquare (χ_F(a) = −1) has χ_K(A) = (−1)^d = 1 exactly when d is even. In F_q[T] terms: a constant is a quadratic residue mod a monic irreducible P iff it is a square in F_q or deg P is even. isSquare_algebraMap_of_even_finrank specializes: every constant (including 0) becomes a square in any even-degree extension — in particular all of F_q is a square in the quadratic extension F_{q²}.
mathContext: $\mathrm{IsSquare}(a \text{ in } K) \iff \mathrm{IsSquare}(a \text{ in } F) \vee 2 \mid [K:F]$; nonsquare $a$ becomes a square in $F_{q^d} \iff 2 \mid d$.
